name: Container
description: The measurements every screen in this library is already making: how wide a page is, how far its content sits from the edge of the column, the three vertical spacings, the responsive column grid, and the rules for what may scroll and in which direction. A reference for the box the other layouts sit in, not a screen of its own.
when_to_use: Reach for this to settle a measurement — what cap a page takes, which gutter goes at which breakpoint, whether the gap between two blocks is 16px or 20px, and what has to be written on a flex child before it will scroll. It is a reference and not a screen: every variant here is one rule shown with enough real content around it to be visible, and none of them is a page you paste whole. When you want an actual screen the entry is a neighbour — form-page for a create or edit screen, index-page for a register, record-page for one record read, dashboard for a strip of figures, settings-page for a long page of preferences — and each of those already carries these measurements in its markup, so copying one of them is copying this. What is left for this entry is the case they do not cover: a screen with no entry of its own, or a question about a value one of them wrote and did not explain. Two neighbours sit close enough to be reached for by mistake. card is the bordered white panel that groups one thing; it is a component with a header, a body and a footer, and the fact that it also fixes the padding inside itself does not make it a spacing primitive — the space between two cards is here, the space inside one is there, and cards do not nest. separator is the rule that divides two blocks, and it is almost always a border on the neighbour rather than an element of its own, so a gap that needed a line is separator and a gap that needed nothing but air is here. Everything outside <main> — the rail, the topbar, the single scrolling column — is app-shell, which is where the outermost of these measurements is already written and where every one of these variants renders.
rules: Nothing here was chosen. Every figure in this entry was counted across the registry first and the majority won, and the counts are written into the variant comments so the next person can recount them rather than trust them. Where the library disagrees with itself the outlier is named rather than quietly overruled.

One gutter, two steps: 16px below lg, 24px at lg and above, written p-4 pb-6 lg:p-6 on a page body and px-4 lg:px-6 on a full-bleed band. Counted, 34 of 34 class strings carrying lg:p-6 pair it with a plain p-4 and 52 of 52 carrying lg:px-6 pair it with px-4, and not one of the 86 takes an sm: or md: step in between. A tablet therefore gets the phone gutter, which is deliberate — a third step buys about four pixels and one more thing to get wrong.

Three page caps, and which one you take is decided by what is inside, not by the section the page belongs to. max-w-[1600px] for anything holding a table or a strip of figures, and it is the value app-shell's own main column already writes. max-w-5xl for a long read-and-edit page. max-w-4xl for a form, and it is the closest thing to a default form-page has. max-w-sm on auth-page is the fourth and it is a card, not a page. 1600px is an arbitrary value because Tailwind's own scale stops at max-w-7xl, 1280px, which is narrower than a fourteen-column ledger wants.

form-page is the outlier worth knowing about: it moves its own cap variant by variant — 3xl for the wizard, 4xl for the default and the invalid state, 5xl for sections, 6xl for the side rail. That is not drift. The cap follows the widest thing the page has to hold, and a form that grew a 320px rail needs 320px more page. Copy the cap from the variant you copied the layout from.

The reading measure is max-w-xl, 576px: a column of form fields takes it, and the exact string max-w-xl space-y-5 appears 22 times. Explanatory prose under a heading caps at max-w-md, 448px, and help text under a control at max-w-sm, 384px. max-w-md and max-w-sm are each written more often than max-w-xl and most of those are not measures at all — they are panels, a dialog or an auth card sized rather than a line length capped — so look at what the class is on before reading a count as a reading width. Four one-off caps are written in ch — 34ch, 38ch, 42ch, 46ch — and every one of them is centred copy on an auth or error page, which is the case where a rem cap would leave a short sentence unbalanced.

Four vertical spacings, and they are not interchangeable. space-y-4 between page sections and between cards; space-y-5 between the fields of a form; space-y-2 between the options of one question; space-y-0.5 between the rows of a dense meta list. The one that surprises people is that the form stack is looser than the page stack. A card has a border doing the grouping, so 16px only has to keep two borders apart; a field is three lines of unbordered text where the whitespace is the only thing saying where one field ends, and at 16px a column of five of them reads as one fifteen-line block.

Column counts step at sm and at xl, never at md. Counted across every responsive grid in the registry: 117 sm:grid-cols-<n>, 25 xl:grid-cols-<n>, 6 lg:grid-cols-<n>, and zero md:grid-cols-<n>. Every md: in the library is md:hidden, md:table, md:table-cell, md:border-r or a named track list — a change of markup rather than a change of column count. That split is the rule: sm and xl move columns, md changes what the markup is, lg moves the gutter.

min-h-0 on every flex item in a scroll chain, and it is the single most repeated fix in this library at over 150 occurrences. A flex item's min-height defaults to auto, so without it a pane will not shrink below its own content, the frame grows past the height you gave it, and the page scrolls with no scrollbar on the thing that was supposed to have one. The siblings that must not scroll take shrink-0 for the mirror reason: flex-shrink defaults to 1, so a forty-row body flattens the totals bar to nothing before the scroller ever engages.

A page inside app-shell does not have its own scroller. The shell is a fixed-height flex frame and its <main id="kon-main" class="min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-auto"> is the one scrolling column in the application, so a band that has to stay put is sticky against that column and never a second overflow-y-auto. The z ladder underneath that: z-10 for a band sticking inside a card or a scrolling list, z-30 for a band sticking across the page, z-40 for menus, popovers and the off-canvas backdrop, z-50 for dialogs, sheets and toasts, and one z-60 in the whole registry, on app-shell's skip link, which has to clear all of them.

The page never scrolls sideways, and every overflow-x-auto in the registry is on a box rather than on the page: sixteen a snapping rail, five a scrollable tab strip, three a genuinely wide table inside its own bordered box, and the rest a row of chips or filters. The default answer for a table on a phone is not a sideways scroller at all — it is table/responsive, two renderings of the same records with the cards shown below md, because a five-column register in a scroller is unusable with a thumb. What actually stops a page growing is min-w-0, which appears over a thousand times: a flex or grid child will not shrink below its intrinsic minimum, so one long vendor name or one <select> as wide as its longest option pushes the whole column past the viewport.

There is no safe-area utility in this library and no variant needs one, because nothing in it is pinned to the bottom edge of the viewport. Every action bar is sticky bottom-0 in the flow of the column it belongs to, so it sits above the browser chrome rather than under the home indicator, and sheet/phone says so in its own comment. The two things that are viewport-fixed keep clear by hand: a toast strip is fixed inset-x-4 bottom-4, and a dialog backdrop is fixed inset-0 p-4, which is the page gutter again. If a screen ever genuinely has to pin a bar to the bottom edge it needs env(safe-area-inset-bottom), which nothing here writes — that is a new pattern and a question for a person, not a value to pick.

Where a page carries a full-bleed band, the gutter box is written twice and the two copies must match. The band runs edge to edge across the column and puts mx-auto max-w-[1600px] px-4 lg:px-6 on its own inner div; the body below it repeats the same cap and the same gutter; <main> itself carries no class at all. Put the cap on <main> instead and the white band stops short of the column edges and reads as a card that lost its border; change one copy and not the other and the h1 sits a few pixels off the first card under it.

anatomy.description: mx-auto max-w-<cap> p-4 pb-6 lg:p-6 — the centred, capped, padded box the page content lives in. On <main> where there is no band, and on each child of <main> where there is one.
The max-width the gutter box takes: 1600px for a register or a dashboard, 5xl for a long settings page, 4xl for a form. Chosen from what the page holds.
max-w-xl inside the cap, for a column of form fields; max-w-md for explanatory prose; max-w-sm for help text. A cap inside a cap, because a card may be 900px wide and its fields must not be.
space-y-4 on the gutter box. Sections and cards take the same number; the stacks inside them do not.
grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2 xl:grid-cols-4 for a strip of tiles, grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 for a pair of fields. Every item takes min-w-0.
min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto on the part that scrolls, shrink-0 on the header and footer that do not. Only inside a frame with a height of its own.
sticky top-0 z-30 on a page band, sticky bottom-0 on an action bar, both in the flow of app-shell's scrolling column. Opaque, and bordered on the edge the content passes.
overflow-x-auto overscroll-x-contain on the box around a genuinely wide table, with a min-w on the table itself. The box, never the page.
p-4 at 390px — 16px each side, 358px of content — and the same 2rem the floating panels subtract with max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)].

behaviour: Nothing here moves on its own. Every variant is static markup, because a measurement that needed JavaScript to hold would not be a measurement.
The gutter changes once, at lg. Below it the page is padded 16px on three sides and 24px at the bottom; at lg and above it is 24px all round. There is no step at sm and none at md.

The cap stops the content and the page keeps going. Past 1600px on a register, or 896px on a form, the gutter box centres and the zinc-100 page ground fills the rest — the content does not stretch and the gutters do not grow.
Column counts drop at sm and at xl. A four-tile strip is one column on a phone, two from 640px and four from 1280px, and it is never three.

Shape changes at md, and only markup changes there: a table swaps for a list of cards, a two-pane layout becomes two screens, a queue pane leaves the flow. Nothing changes its column count at that width.

A region scrolls only inside a frame that has a height. Inside app-shell the frame is the shell, the scroller is its main column, and a page that adds a second one traps the wheel in a box the user cannot see the edges of.
A sticky band stays put against the column it is in, not against the viewport, so it is still correct when the same markup is dropped inside a dialog or a sheet.
A wide table scrolls inside its own box and takes the page nowhere with it. overscroll-x-contain stops the gesture that ran off the end of the table from turning into a browser back swipe.

At 390px every variant here holds without scrolling sideways: the grids are one column, the tables are cards, the bands wrap their actions onto a second line and the caps are all wider than the screen so none of them is doing anything.
accessibility: One <main> per page and one <h1> inside it, in the page header. The container is not a landmark of its own: a div that only sets a width and a padding has no role and needs none.

A full-bleed band at the top of a page is a <header> inside <main>, not a banner landmark. The banner belongs to app-shell's topbar, and a second one on the page gives a landmark list two of them and no way to tell which is the application.

Regions below the h1 are <section> elements with an aria-labelledby pointing at their own h2, so the heading outline is the page's table of contents and the landmark list is not padded with unnamed regions.

A scroll region that is not focusable is unreachable by keyboard in Firefox and Safari, so a min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto box holding no controls takes tabindex="0" and a name. One holding a list of links or rows does not — the controls inside it are what the keyboard scrolls with.
A sideways scroller needs the same treatment for the same reason, and it also needs a name, because "scrollable region" on its own tells nobody what they are in.

A sticky band must not cover the thing a fragment link just scrolled to. Landing focus behind an opaque bar reads to a sighted keyboard user as a link that did nothing, so a page with a sticky band gives its targets scroll-margin-top or puts the band in the flow.
The gutter is not decoration. 16px each side at 390px is what keeps a focus outline — outline-3 at outline-offset-2, so five pixels beyond the control — from being clipped by the edge of the screen.
Nothing in this entry announces anything, which is the point: a container that had a role, a name or a live region would be describing a box rather than the content in it.
